slides.title: Why churn is rising
Churn is rising almost only in SMB, where the monthly rate jumped by more than half in a year

claims.claim: Churn is rising almost only in SMB, where the monthly rate jumped by more than half in a year
evidence: Monthly logo churn H1 2025 / H1 2026: SMB 2.0% / 3.1%; Mid-market 0.6% / 0.8%; Enterprise 0.2% / 0.2%
55% relative rise in SMB monthly logo churn in a year

claims.claim: The churn problem sits where customers can leave at any time
evidence: SMB: self-serve monthly and annual plans, and the only segment where Inkwell competes head-on
Mid-market: a small rise on annual contracts, still a quarter of the SMB rate
Enterprise: flat on multi-year contracts

claims.claim: logo churn overstates the revenue at risk
evidence: SMB is 80% of customers but 24% of ARR

claims.claim: The board dashboard's "1.4% → 2.3%" is undefined and matches no segment measure (backup); this deck uses segment logo churn throughout

slides.title: The 2025 promotion explains the SMB rise: customers outside it churn at 2.1%, almost the same as a year ago

claims.claim: The 2025 promotion explains the SMB rise: customers outside it churn at 2.1%, almost the same as a year ago
evidence: SMB monthly logo churn: Non-promotion SMB H1 2025 2.0%; Non-promotion SMB H1 2026 2.1%; All SMB H1 2026 3.1%; Promotion cohort H1 2026 4.91%

claims.claim: One cohort drives most of the losses
evidence: 56.4% of SMB customers lost each month came through the 2025 promotion
Promotion cohort: 36% of SMB customers, churning at 2.3 times the rate of the rest

claims.claim: Timing: most of the cohort's leavers went within two months of the 50% discount ending
How we derived the cohort's churn
evidence: 182.9 SMB customers lost a month: 3.1% × 5,900
− 79.8 lost from outside the promotion: 2.1% × 3,800
÷ 2,100 promotion customers in the base
= 4.9% implied monthly churn of the cohort

claims.claim: Everyone else: no sign that price or product has worn out with established SMB customers

slides.title: The promotion cohort cites price because it never adopted the product, activating at little more than half the usual rate

claims.claim: Price complaints rose only through the promotion cohort
evidence: Churners naming price as main reason: All SMB H1 2025 19%; All SMB H1 2026 34%; Non-promotion SMB H1 2026 18%; Promotion cohort H1 2026 52%

claims.claim: Fewer than half of the cohort set the product up in month one
evidence: New customers sending 5+ documents in month one: Promotion cohort 41%; Other cohorts 72%

claims.claim: Low first-month use triples churn, so activation, not price, is this cohort's lever

slides.title: The CFO's across-the-board rise
Only about $7.6M of the CFO's $10.3M can land in 2027, because a quarter of it renews later or is capped

evidence: 12% on all ARR $10.32M; Mid-market renewing after 2027 −$0.738M; Enterprise renewing after 2027 −$1.728M; Enterprise caps at 7% −$0.288M; Reachable in 2027 $7.566M
$86.0M × 12% = $10.3M, the CFO's figure

claims.claim: Contracts, not customers, cut the headline
evidence: 26.7% of the CFO's $10.3M cannot land in 2027

claims.claim: Enterprise: the largest cut, since 60% of its ARR renews after 2027
Mid-market: 15% of its ARR renews after 2027 and takes the rise in 2028
SMB: renews in full in 2027, so it supplies 33% of what remains, all from the segment where churn is rising

evidence: List price $ per user per month: Inkwell Starter 9; Palisade SMB today 15; Palisade SMB after +12% 16.8; Inkwell Pro 24; Palisade Business 29

claims.claim: Since Starter launched, we lose most SMB deals where Inkwell is in the running
evidence: Win rate in SMB deals where Inkwell was considered: H1 2025 51%; H1 2026 38%
−13 pp
Inkwell launched Starter in October 2025

claims.claim: The rise lands on the segment where Inkwell competes, on top of a cohort that left when its last price step came

slides.title: Where a rise can work
Larger customers can carry a rise: they retain 112% and 118% of revenue, and a price test barely moved sign-ups

claims.claim: Expansion outweighs churn (mid-market)
evidence: 112% mid-market net revenue retention
Customers name integrations and the audit trail as their main reasons to stay
Inkwell has not been seen in deals above 200 seats; smaller mid-market deals are the exposed edge
85% of mid-market ARR renews in 2027, so most of a rise lands this year

claims.claim: The stickiest customers we have (enterprise)
evidence: 118% enterprise net revenue retention
Same integration and audit-trail reasons to stay
60% of enterprise ARR is capped at 7% a year
Only 40% renews in 2027; the rest takes a rise later

claims.claim: Buyers barely noticed a 10% rise
evidence: −0.5 pp change in mid-market conversion at +10% list price, not significant
2024 test on new sign-ups: 23.1% converted, against 23.6% in the control group

claims.claim: Existing customers at renewal were not tested, so the first 2027 renewals are the real test
evidence: 12% is above the tested 10%

slides.title: As a result, the mid-market rise pays for itself unless monthly churn more than doubles, to about 1.7%

claims.claim: the mid-market rise pays for itself unless monthly churn more than doubles, to about 1.7%
evidence: 0.8% mid-market monthly logo churn today (H1 2026)
+ 0.9 pp extra monthly churn the rise can absorb: $4.2M added ÷ ($39.0M renewing ARR at the new price × 12 months)
= 1.7% breakeven churn: 2.1 times today's rate

claims.claim: the 15% growth target is lost much earlier, at about 1.0% a month

slides.title: Outside the promotion cohort, an 8% SMB rise would still net about $0.7M if customers react as they did in 2023

claims.claim: an 8% SMB rise would still net about $0.7M if customers react as they did in 2023
evidence: $1.3M added: 8% on $16.6M of SMB ARR outside the promotion, all renewing in 2027
−$0.6M lost at the 2023 reaction: churn +0.5 pp for six months, +0.1 pp after (3.6% of ARR)
$0.7M kept; the rise loses money only if the reaction is 2.1 times 2023's

claims.claim: 8% is the one SMB rise we have measured; 12% would put the plan at $16.80 against Inkwell's $9, and its reaction is unknown
Their churn and price complaints have not moved since 2025
evidence: churn 2.1% compared with 2.0%
price complaints 18% compared with 19%

The recommended mix keeps most of the CFO's upside while sparing the customers most likely to leave over price

evidence: CFO plan 16.6%: ($8.0M retention + $7.6M − $1.3M SMB response) ÷ $86.0M

slides.title: Activating the promotion cohort is worth up to $1.0M of ARR and a third off SMB churn, not the half promised

claims.claim: Activating the promotion cohort is worth up to $1.0M of ARR
evidence: $4.4M ARR of the 2,100 promotion customers at full price
× 22.9 pp more of them still with us after 12 months at 2.1% monthly churn than at 4.9% (77.5% against 54.7%)
= $1.01M ARR kept in 2027 at best, before the programme's cost

evidence: Best case: the cohort churns like other SMB customers from January, cutting SMB churn from 3.1% to 2.1%, by 32%
Halving SMB churn to 1.55% would need the cohort to churn at 0.56% a month, a quarter of the rate of established SMB customers

slides.title: Existing customers would just clear the $98.9M target in 2027 if retention holds, leaving new business as the only buffer

claims.claim: Base clears the target by $0.8M; stress does not
evidence: ARR today 86; SMB at 94% NRR −1.26; Mid-market at 112% NRR +4.92; Enterprise at 118% NRR +4.32; Mid-market +12% +4.182; Enterprise at contract terms +0.864; SMB outside promotion +8%, net +0.6826; 2027, existing customers 99.7086
$86M + $7.98M segments at trailing NRR + $5.05M MM and enterprise + $0.7M SMB +8%, net = $99.7M before new customers
Stress: mid-market churn up by half; SMB NRR without the promotion step-up: $95.6M = $99.7M − $1.9M (0.4 pp × 12 × $39.0M) − $2.2M ($4.4M × 50%)

claims.claim: NRR: 116% in the base and 111% in stress, above the 100% floor
High: $100.7M if the promotion cohort is fully activated
Stress gap: about $3.3M, for new business to cover

slides.title: Five gates let leadership scale the plan back before any rise costs more than it earns

claims.claim: Five gates let leadership scale the plan back before any rise costs more than it earns
evidence: SMB NRR definition | Counts the promotion step-up (up to $2.2M) | Before approval, Dec 2026 | Plan on the stress case and size new-business targets to the gap
Mid-market monthly churn, renewed accounts | 0.97% | End of Q1 2027 | 15% at risk: raise new-business and activation targets
Mid-market monthly churn, renewed accounts | 1.7% | End of Q1 and Q2 2027 | Rise no longer pays: hold remaining renewals at 7%
Non-promotion SMB monthly churn | 2.6% | End of Q1 2027 | Above the 2023 reaction: stop the 8% for remaining SMB renewals
Promotion-cohort monthly churn | 3.5% | End of Q2 2027 | Activation is not working: stop extra onboarding spend, keep the price flat
Thresholds: 1.0% uses up the base case's $0.8M headroom; 1.7% is the mid-market breakeven; 2.6% is today's 2.1% plus the 2023 rise of 0.5 pp; 3.5% is halfway from the cohort's 4.9% to 2.1%

claims.claim: Every gate is checked by mid-2027, early enough to change the second half of the year's renewals

assumptions_and_uncertainties: Cohort churn is derived from the segment and non-promotion rates with mid-2026 customer counts as weights; the pack does not report it directly
The board dashboard's "1.4% → 2.3%" is undefined and matches no segment measure
Exit survey covers churned customers who answered it; "price" = main reason "price / found a cheaper option"
Assumes the 60% of enterprise ARR under 7% caps is spread evenly across renewal years; $7.6M is before any churn response to the rise
Net revenue retention as reported in the briefing pack (definition not given)
Existing customers at renewal were not tested, so the first 2027 renewals are the real test; 12% is above the tested 10%

Breakeven simplifications: lost ARR ≈ extra monthly churn × 12 months × renewing ARR at the new price (simple, not compounded); customers who leave over price are of average size; expansion stays at today's rate, only churn reacts; mid-market churn starts from its H1 2026 level of 0.8%
SMB rise: the extra churn is applied to all of their ARR at the new $16.20 price for twelve months; based on the 2023 reaction
Growth = trailing NRR by segment plus price uplift, net of the SMB churn response, before new customers. CFO row: 2023 reaction scaled by 12 ÷ 8 on all SMB ARR, generous for the promotion cohort
Enterprise at 7% on capped and 12% on other ARR renewing in 2027 in every row
The onboarding programme's cost is not in the briefing pack and is not netted out
Whether the cohort can be activated at all is one of the pack's open questions; the gates track it
SMB's 94% NRR may include the cohort's step from 50% off to full price; the pack does not define NRR, so stress removes up to $2.2M
Stress case: mid-market churn up by half; SMB NRR without the promotion step-up; stress gap about $3.3M for new business to cover
